newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil steady.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil and gas oil swaps market were steady at midday on Wednesday after a more than seven percent one-day price fall on Tuesday as the market took a breather from the recent slump, traders said.
"There is slight technical rebound but the fundamentals have not changed. I can't see any buyers for prompt cargoes," one trader said.
Gas oil swaps opened firmer with February traded at $25.28 and $25.25 per barrel, compared to Tuesday's $25.10/$25.30.
But by midday the rebound lost some steam and the market was last quoted at $25.15/$25.25, brokers said.
March was quoted at $25.50/$25.75, up from Monday's $25.40/$25.60 as the February/March contango widened to last quote at minus 50/30 cents.
But traders said the contango needed to widen further for people to buy prompt cargoes.
In the past two weeks, physical gas oil prices in Singapore have slumped more than $6.00 per barrel, or about 20 percent, while fuel oil has lost around $28 per tonne, or 22 percent.
February fuel oil swaps were last quoted unchanged from Monday at $95.00/$96.00 a tonne. The market traded to a low of $95.50 a tonne on Monday night, one broker said.
March offers were quoted at $96.25/$97.75 per tonne, also largely unchanged.
The February/March time spread widened to trade on Tuesday night at minus $1.25 a tonne, compared with an earlier trade of minus $1.00.
Traders said both gas oil and fuel oil markets were bearish due to scarce demand from China and high stocks at terminals in Hong Kong, China as well as build up of inventories in Singapore.
Sellers were hard pushed to find a market for their prompt cargoes, they said. Faced with growing speculation of defaults by Chinese buyers, the market was extremely nervous, traders said.
